message:
docs(observe): record the rule, the dependency, and what was not tested

One pass over the whole observe/https change: history #482, the plan's
server-settings section, and the ledger.

Three things it would be easy to leave out, so they are stated where someone
looking for them will find them:

The evidence for TLS is not one thing. Certificate rejection was executed
against a self-signed fixture. The redirect refusal is a runtime option read
back off a live session, not a redirect that was actually refused -- from an
untrusted fixture the handshake fails first, so an assertion there would be
green whether or not the policy existed. TLS 1.2 has source evidence only,
because that option cannot be read back at all. And no valid https exchange
has ever succeeded here, which means a transport that refused everything
would pass the file. Written as four rows rather than one sentence.

Switching to https is not an nginx change. The server app must advertise the
observe endpoint and both clients must read it: an old server refuses new
https clients (with a reason), and a new server does not save an old client,
which still computes 444. Both directions are in the doc, because "put TLS
in front of it" is exactly what someone would try.

And the origin comparison changes what an existing install does. Hosts that
re-registered on every heartbeat because of a trailing slash will stop; an
address changed from http to https now needs a fresh sign-in and
registration. The second one is deliberate -- a token issued to one origin
is not sent to another -- so it is recorded as intended rather than as a
regression someone will later try to fix.
